m24.content:
Diagnosis: `com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessCommonJSModules.normalizeSourceName(java.lang.String)` is the buggy method.

Why:
- The failing input is `foo\\baz.js`.
- The constructor normalizes `filenamePrefix` to `foo/` because `MODULE_SLASH` is `/`.
- [`guessCJSModuleName`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessCommonJSModules.java:71 ) just calls `toModuleName(normalizeSourceName(filename))`.
- [`normalizeSourceName`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessCommonJSModules.java:116 ) does not convert backslashes to forward slashes before checking the prefix:
  - it tests `filename.indexOf(filenamePrefix) == 0`
  - with `filename = "foo\\baz.js"` and `filenamePrefix = "foo/"`, that check fails
  - it then returns the original Windows-style path unchanged
- [`toModuleName`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ProcessCommonJSModules.java:88 ) only replaces `/`, not `\`, so it produces `module$foo\baz` instead of stripping `foo/` and returning `module$baz`.

The in-code comment in `normalizeSourceName` also confirms the intended behavior: it says DOS may normalize `/` to `\`, but the method never performs that conversion.

Dynamic verification was attempted, but the debugger reported the nominated lines were unreached, so this conclusion is based on static analysis and the exact failure shape.
